tasks.short: Turn the board's and Finance Director's budget guidelines into budget rules and instructions for site and cost-centre managers.

today.trigger: The annual budget round starts, or the board or Finance Director issues a mid-year directive (a cost freeze, a flex-hours cap, a new CAO wage step).
steps: Read the directive in the board memo or email and agree what it means with the Finance Director
Work out the effect on each site (Rotterdam, Tilburg, Venlo) and cost centre in Excel
Write the budget instructions and rules (wage index, flex ratio, capex limits) in Word and the planning template
Send them to site managers and answer their questions by mail and Teams
Check that submitted budgets follow the rules and chase the ones that don't
drudgery: Rewriting the same instruction for three sites and many cost centres
Answering the same questions from managers one by one
Checking submitted templates line by line against the rules
today.time_sinks: Back-and-forth with managers who read the directive differently, and manual checks of submitted budgets against the rules.

lenses.faster: An assistant drafts the instruction pack and a per-site impact table from the directive and last year's pack; the analyst edits instead of writing from scratch.
lenses.autonomous: Once rules are written as checks in the template, each submitted budget is tested on arrival and the manager gets a list of breaches without the analyst opening it.
lenses.ambitious: Every directive gets a written rule set with an owner and a version, so budget policy is consistent across sites and auditable for the first time.
lenses.joy: No more retyping the same rules and chasing format errors; what is left is the conversation about what the board actually wants.
lenses.options: For an ambiguous directive, draft two or three readings with their euro effect per site so the Finance Director chooses before managers start.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns the rule book and the checks in the planning template, not the individual instructions and reviews.
reach: Controller: budget control rules that feed the month-end variance checks
HR Business Partner: headcount and flex-ratio rules in the workforce plan

tasks.human_edge: Knowing what the board and Finance Director mean, and holding the line with site managers when a rule hurts their plan.
tasks.pattern_why: Interpreting a directive is judgement and negotiation; AI drafts instructions and impact tables, while rule checks on submitted budgets are deterministic software.

in_practice.trigger: A budget directive is saved to the Finance SharePoint budget folder.
steps: Assistant reads the directive and last year's instruction pack and drafts the new instructions and a list of open questions
Analyst and Finance Director settle the open questions and pick the reading
Rules are coded as checks in the Excel budget template
Submitted budgets are checked on upload and breaches are listed for the manager
An FAQ draft answers recurring manager questions, reviewed by the analyst
in_practice.human_gate: The Finance Director approves the interpretation and the instruction pack before it goes to sites.
data_needed: Last year's instruction pack and template
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint budget folder with versioned rule book and a check log per submission

evidence.claim: Finance executives report budgeting as the task where AI was most often more useful than expected (net +42), while judgement-heavy tasks gain least.
Speed without defined drivers and encoded policies makes existing errors harder to catch.
An LLM can draft instruction packs and FAQs from a directive and last year's pack.

risks: A wrong reading of the directive spreads to every site faster
Managers treat the AI-drafted FAQ as policy without Finance review
Rule checks harden last year's assumptions without anyone noticing
research_questions: How many hours did the last budget round spend on instructions, questions and rule checks?
Can the budget rules be written as checks in the current Excel template, or does that need a planning tool?
How often did managers misread last year's directive, and what did that cost in rework?

tasks.short: Build cost-benefit cases, like lease or buy trucks, warehouse automation, or flex versus own staff, and review requests.

today.trigger: A site manager, the board or the Finance Director asks for a business case or financing comparison, or a capex request arrives.
steps: Collect costs, volumes and quotes from the requester, AFAS and supplier offers
Build a cash-flow and NPV model in Excel
Compare financing options (lease, Rabobank loan, own cash)
Test a few sensitivities by hand
Write a memo or slides with a recommendation
drudgery: Rebuilding a model from a blank sheet for each case
today.time_sinks: Gathering inputs and rebuilding the model; only one or two scenarios get tested because each one is manual.

lenses.faster: A standard model template with fixed drivers fills itself from AFAS actuals and the request form; the analyst reviews assumptions instead of building.
lenses.autonomous: A capex request on the standard form triggers a first-pass model and a list of missing or odd inputs, ready before the analyst opens it.
lenses.ambitious: Every request above a threshold gets a proper case with sensitivity and a post-investment check a year later, which few get today.
lenses.joy: No more blank-sheet models and chasing numbers; the analyst spends time on the assumptions that decide the answer.
lenses.options: Each case shows three to five options (do nothing, lease, buy, phase in, flex instead of hire) with NPV, cash and risk side by side.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns the template, the drivers and the review rules, and audits cases rather than building each one.
reach: Controller: capex approval checks and post-investment reviews
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: cost of own staff versus agency flex workers

tasks.human_edge: Judging which assumptions are credible, what the requester is not saying, and which risk the company can carry.
tasks.pattern_why: The calculation is deterministic once drivers are fixed, but choosing assumptions and the recommendation needs judgement; AI builds options and drafts, the analyst leads.

in_practice.trigger: A request is submitted on the business-case form in SharePoint.
steps: Template pulls actuals from the AFAS extract and fills the model
Assistant flags missing inputs and outliers against past cases
Model runs the option set and sensitivities
Assistant drafts a memo with the options table and caveats
Analyst reviews assumptions, edits and signs off
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst signs off the model and memo; the Finance Director or board decides.
data_needed: Financing terms from the bank and lessors
Agency rates and CAO wage costs
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint case register with model version, assumptions and decision

evidence.claim: Model building (net +27) and scenario planning (net +26) were more often more useful than expected with AI.
Agents run scenario mechanics and draft commentary while people allocate capital.
Workpapers built in personal chatbots cannot be rebuilt for the auditor, so models must live in the shared template.

risks: Polished output hides weak assumptions supplied by the requester
Models built in personal chatbots cannot be audited
More cases are requested because they are cheap, without better decisions
research_questions: How many business cases and capex requests did FP&A handle last year, and how long did each take?
Can one template cover most cases (vehicles, warehouse equipment, staffing), or are they too different?
How did past cases compare with actual results a year later?

tasks.short: Look for cost savings and margin gains, like overtime, agency hours, idle trucks, per site.

today.trigger: A margin dip, a board request, or the analyst spots something in the monthly figures.
steps: Pull costs and volumes per site from Power BI and AFAS
Compare agency invoices and hours from the staffing portals
Look for outliers in Excel (overtime, absence, cost per pallet or per km)
Discuss findings with site managers and the Controller
Write up ideas with estimated savings
drudgery: Merging agency portal exports with AFAS data by hand
Building the same comparison tables each month
today.time_sinks: Joining data from AFAS, agency portals and Power BI; most time goes to preparing data, little to finding causes.

lenses.faster: A monthly join of AFAS, agency hours and invoices, and volumes shows cost per unit and outliers per site, ready to read.
lenses.autonomous: Outliers above a set threshold, such as agency hours above plan or invoice hours not matching ordered hours, are flagged to the analyst and site manager automatically.
lenses.ambitious: Every site gets a monthly driver review with a tracked list of savings ideas and their realised euros, instead of ad hoc hunts.
lenses.joy: No more spreadsheet merging; time goes to site visits and working out with managers why a number moves.
lenses.options: For each finding, the assistant drafts several possible causes and actions with rough euro effects to test with the site.
lenses.altitude: The analyst defines the cost drivers and thresholds and runs the savings pipeline, rather than hunting for outliers by hand.
reach: Bookkeeper: agency invoice versus hours checks
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: overtime and absence cost analysis

tasks.human_edge: Understanding operations on the floor and persuading site managers to change how they work.
tasks.pattern_why: The data join and outlier flags are deterministic, but finding real causes and winning support for change are human work; AI widens the search and drafts options.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS extract and monthly agency invoice upload complete.
steps: Pipeline joins AFAS costs, agency hours and invoices, and volumes per site
Rules flag outliers against thresholds and plan
Assistant drafts possible causes and questions per flag
Analyst checks with the site manager and records the idea in the savings tracker
Realised savings are measured in the following months
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst decides which flags become savings ideas; site managers and the Finance Director approve actions.
data_needed: AFAS costs and hours per cost centre
in_practice.logs_to: Savings tracker in SharePoint with flag, idea, owner and realised euros

evidence.claim: Agents gather data and flag records that do not tie; people decide what to act on.
Copilot in Power BI can answer questions and summarise reports on a prepared semantic model, with English as the supported language.
Data quality is the top barrier to AI in finance (40.4%).

risks: Overtime and absence data per person is personal data under AVG; works council involvement is needed if it monitors staff
Flags without context lead to blame instead of improvement
Agency data formats differ across the three portals and break the join
research_questions: Can hours and invoices from all three agency portals be exported in a stable format?
How much did agency invoice versus hours mismatches cost last year?
Does the works council need to give consent (WOR art. 27) for site-level overtime and absence analysis?

role.altitude: The FP&A Analyst stops assembling budgets, cases and savings lists and instead owns the drivers, definitions, rule book and forecast rules that templates and assistants run on.
reach: Controller: variance checks, capex control and margin analysis per site
Bookkeeper: agency invoice versus hours matching
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: workforce cost and flex-ratio analysis
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: own staff versus agency cost comparisons
role.ceiling_note: Limited by the nightly AFAS extract, unclear drivers, three different agency portal formats and Power BI Copilot needing a prepared model and English. Board and bank talks, budget negotiations with site managers and capital decisions stay human; about a third of hours can be freed.
skills_to_grow: Driver-based planning and defining drivers per site
Writing budget rules as testable checks
Power BI semantic models and DAX
Prompting and reviewing AI drafts with traceable sources
AVG and works council basics for workforce data
role.ambitious_version: Monthly rolling forecasts and scenarios per site on agreed drivers, every capex case tracked to realised results, and a standing savings pipeline with euros measured, improving forecast accuracy and cutting days to close.
